subject: science
passage: Naked mole-rats, small burrowing rodents of East Africa, live underground in colonies that can include more than a hundred members. Only one female, the queen, gives birth. The other members of the colony have different jobs. Some dig tunnels and gather the roots and tubers that the colony eats, while larger individuals guard the colony against snakes and other intruders.
stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To argue that naked mole-rats are the most social mammals on Earth
choices.B: To describe how work is divided among members of a naked mole-rat colony
choices.C: To describe the snakes that threaten naked mole-rat colonies
choices.D: To explain how naked mole-rats dig tunnels through hard soil

explanation.why: After introducing the colonies, the text explains who does what: the queen gives birth, some members dig and gather food, and larger ones guard the colony. The text is organized around this division of jobs.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text never compares naked mole-rats with other mammals.
explanation.B: Correct. The text describes the different roles of the queen, the diggers and gatherers, and the guards.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Snakes are mentioned only as intruders that the guards defend against; they are not the focus.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Digging is listed as one job, but the text does not explain how the digging is done.
